Pulmonology · published research

Lung fibrosis

Two mouse studies reported reduced collagen or airway-remodeling measures after PBM. The 2017 bleomycin model also showed lower inflammatory and fibrotic measures and improved pulmonary elastance; no clinical study was identified.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Two mouse studies reported reduced collagen or airway-remodeling measures after PBM. The 2017 bleomycin model also showed lower inflammatory and fibrotic measures and improved pulmonary elastance; no clinical study was identified.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Respiratory system > Lung fibrosis category contains two mouse experiments and no human clinical study. One publication also reports an in-vitro cell arm, so the cell result is part of one translational paper rather than a third independent study.

Human and clinical evidence

No clinical PBM study for lung fibrosis was identified in the assigned category.

Animal evidence

In a bleomycin-induced mouse model, Brochetti et al. reported lower inflammatory-cell counts, collagen deposition, interstitial thickening, and pulmonary elastance after photobiomodulation (2017). De Brito et al. also reported reduced inflammatory and airway-remodeling measures in a murine fibrosis model (2020). Both studies are preclinical and cannot establish improvement in lung function or disease progression in patients.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

The second publication also tested lung structural cells in vitro and reported cytokine responses. It is a laboratory arm of the same title, not an independent clinical result. No ex-vivo human lung tissue study is listed.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The mouse study reported red 660-nm light at 5 J/cm2, 100 mW, for 150 seconds over eight daily treatments. Wavelength is the color band of the light and affects tissue penetration. The two animal studies use different models and should not be treated as one standardized exposure.

Interpretation

The data support further experimental work on selected inflammatory and fibrotic measures. They do not show that PBM slows fibrosis or improves symptoms in people. Replication across models and careful dose reporting are needed before clinical efficacy can be judged.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low for reduced inflammatory and fibrosis-related measures in two mouse experiments No direct human evidence identified
Publications and records2 titles (exact Respiratory system > Lung fibrosis)

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Both records are mouse experiments, and one also includes a laboratory cell arm. Neither tests people with pulmonary fibrosis. Independent models should reproduce functional and tissue outcomes before carefully staged patient studies assess safety, lung function, symptoms, and disease progression.
